newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: DE BEERS H1 DIAMOND SALES UP 4.8 PCT.
newsitem.headline: DE BEERS H1 DIAMOND SALES UP 4.8 PCT.

text.p: De Beers Central Selling Organisation announced on Wednesday sales of rough gem diamonds rose 4.81 percent to a record U.S.$2.88 billion in the first six months of 1997.
In rand terms, sales amounted to 12.92 billion rand, 1.98 billion rand or 18.04 percent up on the first half of 1996.
Second half sales were expected to be lower, however, reflecting the usual relationship between first and second half sales, it said in a statement.
The Central Selling Organisation (CSO), De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd's selling arm, said sales in the first half reflected the strength of its distribution network and increased market share.

"Russian export licensing delays have served to limit Russian exports and there has been reduced Angolan rough diamond activity as a result of the security situaion and higher than normal seasonal rainfall," the company said.
The civil war in the former Zaire had also disrupted supplies to the outside market.

The company said consumer trends indicated that U.S. demand was continuing to grow at a similar rate to last year, while Japan, the second largest market after the U.S., was still expected to have a difficult year.
It noted, however, that first quarter sales of diamond jewellery in Japan were up in advance of retail tax increases in April.
"Europe is still mixed, with the U.K. and Germany showing rising sales, while sales in France and Italy are more sluggish," it said.

It added that while Korea was reported to be flat in the first quarter, Taiwan appeared to be recovering, with diamond jewellery sales up a little in the first three months of this year -- the first rise in two years -- and expectations of stronger growth for the rest of the year.
